### Section: Know—may God guide us and you—that the Moon traverses one mansion every day
And it traverses a zodiac sign in approximately two and one-third days. This has been mentioned previously—
<note>The author refers to the "Lunar Mansions" (Manazil al-Qamar), a system of 28 divisions of the sky used in medieval Islamic astronomy to track the Moon's position.</note>
meaning the mansions and their boundaries within the zodiac signs. I shall mention the twelve zodiac signs
and the twenty-eight mansions, and how the Moon traverses them during its journey over the course of
a month of approximately thirty days. I have set this out in tables to make it easier for you
to memorize them when you look at them. I will provide you with an example of this. **An example:** Suppose
the Moon is in the mansion of *al-Sharatan* <note>The "Two Signs," the first lunar mansion, corresponding to the horns of Aries.</note>, which is the first of the mansions of the sign of Aries. It remains
before setting for **1** and **11** sevenths <note>The author uses a specific fractional system for timekeeping, likely related to seasonal hours.</note> and then sets; this is one hour, one-sixth
of an hour, and one-sixtieth of an hour. On the second night, it will be in the mansion of *al-Butayn* <note>The "Little Belly," the second lunar mansion in Aries.</note>.
It remains before setting for **2** and **8** sevenths and then sets <unclear>two hours</unclear>
<unclear>and a sixth</unclear> <unclear>of an hour</unclear> <unclear>and quarters</unclear> <unclear>of an hour</unclear>. On the third night, it will be
in the mansion of *al-Thurayya* <note>The Pleiades, the third lunar mansion.</note>. It then departs from Taurus and remains before
setting for **3** and **9** sevenths and then sets; this is three hours
and three-quarters of one-fifth of an hour. Follow this calculation and you shall be guided.
**And know**—may God guide us and you—that the Moon rises on the first night of the second half
of the month when **1** and **11** sevenths of the night have passed, which is one hour,
one-sixth of an hour, and one-sixtieth of an hour. It continues its cycle until the end of that night,
where it will be in the mansion of *al-Ghafr* <note>The "Covering," the fifteenth lunar mansion, located in Virgo/Libra.</note> at the beginning of the sign of Libra, approximately. God knows best what is correct.
The explanation here is lengthy, and I have only omitted the full explanation so that it does not become too difficult to memorize. I shall
draw tables for you and write headings for them so that it is easy for you to memorize them when

<margin>
<unclear>On knowing the boundaries of the seven planets</unclear>
</margin>

The twelve [signs]: Know—may God guide us and you—that the seven wandering planets <note>The "seven wandering planets" or *al-kawākib al-sayyārah* refer to the celestial bodies visible to the naked eye in antiquity: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon.</note> are named as follows: the first of them is **Saturn**, then **Jupiter**, **Mars**, the **Sun**, **Venus**, **Mercury**, and the **Moon**. The Sun and the Moon do not have "boundaries" <term>Boundaries (Arabic: *al-hudūd*): also known as 'terms,' these are specific segments of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</term> within the zodiac signs. As for the other five, each one of them has a boundary within the twelve signs. Every sign consists of thirty degrees, and these thirty degrees are divided among these five planets: **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, **Mars**, **Venus**, and **Mercury**. These are the "Masters of the Boundaries."

Know that in the sign of Aries, **Saturn's** boundary is five degrees, **Jupiter's** boundary is six degrees, **Mars's** boundary is five degrees, **Venus's** boundary is six degrees, and **Mercury's** boundary is eight degrees. Thus, the total becomes thirty degrees, and they possess these degrees within Aries. I have already set this out for you in tables on the face of this leaf <note>The author refers to a diagram or table on the preceding page or the flip side of the current folio</note> before this explanation. I only placed these tables in this book because you might be asked about a person's ascendant, their boundaries, and their degree; having this in your memory will ensure you are guided to the right answer.

### Chapter on Knowing the Aspects of the Ascendants and the Faces

Know—may God guide us and you—that the zodiac signs correspond to the degrees of the firmament, which are 360 degrees. There are 36 "faces" <term>Faces (Arabic: *al-wujūh*): also known as 'decans,' these are ten-degree subdivisions of a zodiac sign</term>, meaning thirty-six faces in total. Each face consists of ten degrees, and each face has an "observer" <note>original: *nāẓir*</note> that looks upon it.

**For example**: The sign of Aries is thirty degrees and consists of three faces, having three observers. The first face—meaning the first ten degrees—is under the observation of **Mars**, because he is the Lord of the House <note>Mars is the traditional ruler of Aries</note>. The second face—meaning the second ten degrees—is under the observation of **the Sun**, because the sphere directly below the sphere of Mars is the sphere of the Sun. The third face—meaning the third ten degrees—is under the observation of **Venus**, because the sphere directly below the sphere of the Sun is the sphere of Venus.

Follow this calculation for every observer and face found. If a position does not complete a full ten degrees, it is recorded as a degree within that face. **For example**: you would say to a person, "Your ascendant is Aries, and Mars is at the eighth degree, under the observation of Mars and within the boundary of Venus." Understand this and you shall be guided. I will illustrate tables for this to make it easier for you to memorize in the following part of the leaf.

# Tables of the Great Abjad Calculation <note>The Abjad system is a decimal alphabetic numeral system where each of the 28 letters of the Arabic alphabet is assigned a specific numerical value.</note>

| A | B | J | D | H | W | Z | Ḥ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| One | Two | Three | Four | Five | Six | Seven | Eight |

| Ṭ | Y | K | L | M | N | S | ‘A |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nine | Ten | Twenty | Thirty | Forty | Fifty | Sixty | Seventy |

| F | Ṣ | Q | R | Sh | T | Th | Kh |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Eighty | Ninety | One Hundred | Two Hundred | Three Hundred | Four Hundred | Five Hundred | Six Hundred |

| Dh | Ḍ | Ẓ | Gh |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seven Hundred | Eight Hundred | Nine Hundred | One Thousand |

---

Know—may God guide us and you—that the count of this "Great Abjad" <note>original: "al-jumal al-kabir"</note> ranges from the number one to one thousand. Understand this system well, for it is the one relied upon for calculations, as these numbers enter into all <term>timekeeping operations<note>original: "al-miqatiyat"; refers to the science of calculating prayer times and astronomical alignments</term>. It is also the method used to take the name of the <term>petitioner<note>original: "al-sa'il"; the person asking a question in a divinatory or horary context</term> and the name of his mother to produce the result of the tablet. 

Know that every letter and its corresponding number is written in a cell directly beneath it; however, for these last four letters, their numbers are in the cell behind them. **For example**, the letter *Dhal* [ذ] is one <note>The text here appears to contain a scribal error or a specific local convention, as the table above correctly lists Dhal as 700</note>, the letter *‘Ayn* [ع] is one thousand, the *Alif* [أ] has its mark beneath it, and the *Ghayn* [غ] has its mark behind it. This sequence is read as: *Abjad, Hawwaz, Hutti, Kalaman, Sa'fas, Qarashat, Thakhadh, Dadhagh*. This is the "Abjad" arrangement; understand it and you shall be guided.

**Section**

Know—may God guide us and you—that the sun traverses one degree every day, and it traverses a Zodiac sign in the period of a month, which is thirty days. Thus, the total number of Zodiac signs is twelve, and the number of degrees in the celestial sphere is three hundred and sixty degrees. It completes the circuit of the sphere in the duration of one full year. This is according to approximate calculation. They observed and calculated this based on the number of days in the Coptic months, because the number of days in the Coptic year is three hundred and sixty days, and the number of each Coptic month is thirty days. However, they added five or six days to the Coptic year, and these days are called the days of *al-Nasi* <note>original: "al-Nasi" - these are the epagomenal or "intercalary" days added at the end of the year to align the calendar with the solar cycle</note>.

The reason for this is because the Arabic months begin with the month of Muharram, which is thirty days, and the second is the month of Safar, which is twenty-nine days. Thus, there is a "complete" month and a "deficient" month based on the ruling of the sighting of the crescent moon. Therefore, the year of the Arabs is called <unclear>Lunar</unclear>, and its months consist of one that is full and one that is short from the month of Muharram to the month of Dhu al-Hijjah. They added what remained of these deficient days to the Coptic months and called them <unclear>al-Nasi</unclear>. They applied this intercalation to the Zodiac signs and matched the days of dawn and the basis of the Zodiac degrees to the Coptic intercalary days. At that point, the calculation of dawn and the calculation of the sun's degrees was completed, as previously mentioned at the beginning of this book regarding the rules of the tables.

**And know**—may God guide us and you—that I desired to collect for you in this book the Coptic months, the Zodiac signs, and the degrees of the sun by approximate calculation, so that it may be easier for you to memorize than the previous method. I shall write at the heads of the tables, and I will mention examples of that for you.

**An example:** On the first day of the month of Tut <note>The first month of the Coptic calendar</note>, the sun is at 14 degrees <note>The scribe uses the Abjad numeral "yad" (10+4) for 14</note>, and it is in the <term>6th</term> <note>The scribe uses "Indian" (Arabic) numerals here</note> sign, meaning the sign of Virgo <note>original: "al-Sunbulah" - The Ear of Grain</note>, having already traversed fourteen degrees of it. On the first day of the month of Babah <note>The second month of the Coptic calendar</note>, the sun is at 14 degrees, and it is in the <term>7th</term> sign, meaning the sign of Libra <note>original: "al-Mizan" - The Scales</note>, having traversed fourteen [degrees] at dawn according to this calculation. A full explanation would be too long for a beginner to memorize.

**And know** that the Zodiac signs are written at the heads of the tables in Indian numerals <note>The ancestor of modern Western numerals</note>, and I have expressed them in the middle of the tables in Arabic script; so understand that. This is the form of the tables on the following page.

### Chapter on Knowing Which Zodiac Sign the Moon is in and How Many Degrees it has Traversed
If you wish to do that, take the days of the crescent moon—meaning from the first of the month you are in until the current day. Whatever number of days you have, multiply them by **2** days. From the total days accumulated, assign one sign for every **30** days. Begin counting from the sign in which the sun is currently located. The sign where the calculation ends is the sign the moon is in. The number of degrees it has traversed in that sign is whatever remains that did not reach a full **30** days. Understand, and you shall be guided.

Every thirty degrees equals two hours, and every sign is thirty degrees. Add to this calculation and understand, you shall be guided.

# Chapter on Tables for Identifying the Indian Script

| A | Y | Q | Gh | B | K | R | J |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10 | 100 | 1000 | 2 | 20 | 200 | 3 |
| L | Sh | D | M | T | H | N | Th |
| 30 | 300 | 4 | 40 | 400 | 5 | 50 | 500 |

| 6 | 60 | 600 | 7 | 70 | 700 | 8 | 80 |
| Ḍ | 800 | Ṭ | 9 | Ṣ | 90 | Ẓ | 900 |

Know—may God guide us and you—that these tables correspond to the number of letters in the Indian script <note>The author is likely referring to the "Ghubar" or "Hindi" numerals which evolved into our modern digits, here mapped against the Arabic Abjad system where letters have numerical values</note>. Know that the *Alif* (A) stands for one, and the *Ya* (Y) for ten because there is a zero in the ones place. The *Qaf* (Q) stands for one hundred because there are zeros in two places: the ones and the tens. The *Ghayn* (Gh) stands for one thousand because there are three zeros in the three places, and it is in the rank of the thousands. This is because you <insert>count</insert> ones, tens, hundreds, and <insert>thousands</insert>. This *Ghayn* is associated with glory <note>original: "bi-l-'izz"; this may be a mnemonic or a symbolic association</note>, and its sign is fixed beneath it in this manner.

An **example** of this is to say *AYQGh* <note>A-Y-Q-Gh represents 1, 10, 100, 1000</note>, which is 1111. The first is *Alif* for one, the second is *Ya* for ten, the third is *Qaf* for one hundred, and the fourth is *Ghayn* for one thousand. It is read as <insert>AYQGh</insert>, *BKRJSh*, *DMT*, <unclear>HNSh</unclear>, <unclear>WKhS</unclear>, <unclear>ZGhḌ</unclear>, <unclear>ḤFẒ</unclear>, <unclear>ṬṢẒ</unclear>. <note>These are mnemonic groupings of letters representing units, tens, hundreds, and thousands</note>.

### On Knowing Miles and Farsakhs; May God Guide Us and You
Know that the mile is 4,000 cubits <note>Arabic: *dhira'*; a traditional unit of length based on the forearm</note>, and the cubit is 24 fingers, and the finger is 6 barleycorns <note>The text says 6 but then clarifies "twelve" in the spelled-out number; this likely refers to the width of the grains</note>, and the barleycorn is 6 hairs <note>The text says 6 but then clarifies "ten" in the spelled-out number</note>. These hairs should be taken from the tails of medium-sized horses. Know that the circumference of the Earth is 24,000 miles <note>original: *dur al-ard*</note> according to the mile mentioned previously. One degree of the Earth's degrees is 66 and two-thirds miles. God knows best; understand this and you shall be guided.

### On Knowing the First Day of the Great Month of Ramadan and the Day of Arafat
Based on the Arabic months, know—may God guide us and you—that the fifth day of the month of Muharram <note>The first month of the Islamic lunar calendar</note> will correspond to the day of the Standing <note>The Day of Arafat, the pinnacle of the Hajj pilgrimage</note>, and the sixth day of it will be the first day of the month of Ramadan <note>This refers to a rule of thumb for calculating the start of the fasting month based on the start of the new year</note>. I will mention an example for you.
**An Example** of this: If the first day of Muharram is a Thursday, then its fifth day is Monday, which would be the Day of the Standing at Arafat. The sixth day of Muharram, which is Tuesday, would be the first day of the Great Month of Ramadan. I will illustrate a table for you so you may understand this. These are the tables:

the horizon toward the North; as for the South: this value which the **azimuth** <note>Arabic: *al-samt*, the horizontal angle of a celestial body</note> reaches never exceeds ninety degrees. **As for the Azimuthal Circle**, it is the circle that passes through the zenith <note>the point directly above the observer</note>, the nadir <note>the point directly below the observer</note>, the body of the star, and the point reached by the azimuth on the circle of the horizon. **As for the Arc of Altitude**, it is the arc of this azimuthal circle between the body of the star and the position reached by the azimuth on the circle of the horizon. **As for the Arc of the Complement of Altitude** <note>the co-altitude</note>, it is the remainder of the arc of altitude from this circle, located between the body of the star and the zenith. **As for the Arc of the Complement of Azimuth**, it is a segment of the circle of the horizon between the position reached by the azimuth on the circle of the horizon and where it terminates at ninety degrees.

**As for the Sphere**, it is a solid body bounded by a single surface, inside of which is a point where all lines extending from it to the surface are equal; that point is called the center of the sphere. **As for the Diameter of the Sphere**, it is the straight line that passes through the center of the sphere and terminates at both sides of the surface surrounding the sphere. **As for the Axis of the Sphere**, it is the diameter upon which the sphere rotates, dividing the sphere into two halves. **As for the Belt** <note>the Great Circle or Equator</note>, these are the great parallel circles standing upon the axis at right angles. **As for the Temporal Circles**, they are the temporal circles of the region of the circle of the **Equator** <note>Arabic: *mu'addil al-nahar*, literally 'the leveler of the day'</note> from the region of the highest sphere, containing the two poles of the world and the two poles of the highest sphere. **As for the Circle** which the sun traces by its motion from East to West: if its surface is imagined cutting through the world, there occurs on the surface of the highest sphere a great circle; this circle is called the **Zodiacal Sphere** <note>Arabic: *mintaqat falak al-buruj*</note>, and its poles are the poles of the zodiac.

Therefore, restrain the soul and bring it back through beautiful reproach. Do not exhaust yourself striving for the benefit of others while you are blamed by them and your anxieties continue to chain you. Be reliant upon the Living, the Everlasting <note>original: "al-Hayy al-Qayyum" - two of the Beautiful Names of God</note>. Be patient and do not leave your place, for movement will harm you. Clothe yourself in sincere advice and do not worry about whoever transgresses against you.

O owner of this omen <note>original: "fal" - a divination result or lot</note>, I counsel you to have patience in all circumstances, even if it lasts a long time. I forbid you from haste, for it inherits boredom and excessive gossip. No one who was patient ever regretted it, and no one who hurried ever gained spoil. If you ask about a request, then delay in it is more necessary.

# The Omen of Warning and Conduct

He has told you in this omen <note>Arabic: *fal*—a method of divination or seeking an augury</note> that all evil and misery come from you, so do not be ill-natured. Do not occupy yourself with carrying tales, for everyone who strives in slander <note>Arabic: *namima*—malicious gossip intended to sow discord</note> possesses despicable traits. You have transgressed against them, leaving nothing behind and sparing no one. Therefore, be patient and do not hurry, for with the hasty comes the slip <note>original: *al-zalal*—a mistake or moral lapse caused by rushing</note>. Do not listen to your adversary, nor obey his words. You have begun to dig up things that were and things that never were; you will fall into evil from every direction. Avoid the enmity of your neighbors and beware of misery in your own place. Others have opposed you in your path, and you have become distressed because of your seeking. You have spoken to yourself of traveling because of the harm that has occurred. Evil does not last, so do not carry worries and put your trust in the Living, the Eternal <note>Arabic: *al-Hayy al-Qayyum*—two of the Beautiful Names of God in Islamic tradition</note>. For there is not one of you except that he has a known station. Do not oppose the people of knowledge <note>referring to scholars or those with spiritual insight</note>, or you will fall and never rise again.

# The Omen of the Letters Ayn, Jim, and Ra

It is written in your omen: make your words the best they can be and improve your circumstances. Be attentive to your affairs and do not be deceived by others, lest your goodness be wasted upon the children of the ignoble <note>The "ignoble" or "base-born" refers to those lacking in character or gratitude.</note>. Listen, O seeker of the omen, to your warning: avoid your [current] aim and do not be stubborn <term>Azuwar: a person who is difficult, stubborn, or turns away from the truth</term>. Do not lean upon false speech, and be cautious regarding yourself. 

There is no avoiding what has been divinely decreed <note>original: "al-maqdur" — the destiny already written by God</note>. Comply with what has been judged for you, for this is what the warner has prescribed for you. I see that you have placed yourself in a state of deficiency <note>The text here is partially obscured by a paper repair; "ikhtilal" suggests a state of disorder or lack</note>, yet you have acted kindly toward others and spoken of their good qualities behind their backs. 

The paths of this world are wondrous and its conditions are ordered, yet at all times the son of Adam <note>A common poetic term for humanity</note> is afflicted by it; rarely does he land upon what is right. The wise person is one who walks the safe paths so that their affairs remain straight. Therefore, O seeker of the omen, ask your Lord for safety, for how quickly the days of time <term>Dahr: fate or cyclical time</term> turn over! Listen to this speech and its rulings:

# The Omen of the Letters: 'Ain, Fa, and Ra

It is written for you in your omen: you are lazy, and no good state comes from you. Therefore, cast aside your lethargy and idleness. Commit yourself to high ambition and leave your laziness behind, for laziness corrupts the very foundation <note>original: "jaber" - likely referring to the structural integrity or "mender" of one's work</note> of your labor. 

We see you, O seeker of this omen, demanding much and seeking to multiply your gains, yet you do not listen to any counsel; you fail and remain stubborn. You associate with people amongst whom everything is hidden or revealed <note>meaning they are untrustworthy or unpredictable</note>, and I see you among them in the rank of a loser. You are bewildered in your affairs; you have found fault, acted with arrogance, wandered about, and risen early to no end. 

Be diligent in your matter if you are a seeker; rise up and seek, and you shall be a victor. Put your trust in the Lord of the Easts and the Wests. Do not sit and allow yourself to be broken, lest you return with the others as a loser. Restrain yourself, O owner of this omen, from movement at this time, for affairs are entangled and enemies are lying in wait, ready to clash with you. You must exercise deliberation in this movement; do not draw near, or you will fall into the snare. You must have patience and composure, and accept this advice from me.

# Your Omen

It has been written for you in your omen: Be patient and do not rush, for haste is wicked and perhaps it may bring harm upon you. Delaying and taking one's time brings harmony in affairs. Therefore, O seeker of this omen, you must practice patience <note>Arabic: *sabr*, a central Islamic virtue of steadfastness</note> and do not be restless, for after certain matters occur, other matters follow. What has happened is enough; the wise person rejects what has already passed. Regarding the goal that has been completed, there has been much false talk about you, and the seeking of others through their speech causes you pain. But the matter has returned to safety, so wake up if you were asleep!

Give thanks to God for these noble favors, hold fast to the rope of God <note>A Quranic metaphor for divine protection and community</note>, and be patient, for the entire matter belongs to God. Walk the path of righteousness and put your trust in God, the Lord of all servants, for He will deliver you from the evil of enemies, the envious, the stubborn, and the adversaries. So be patient and trust in God, the Generous and Bountiful. This omen of yours indicates a temporary pause in your circumstances; so rouse your soul and pay close attention.

# Discourse on the Letter Alif (A)
# Discourse on the Letter Ba (B)

Good news! You have been promised blessings, happiness, joy, and ease.
The daughter of what you hope for has arrived at its place; do not worry, O you who sit in distress.
If you have come to ask about the fulfillment of your needs, they shall be met without hardship or toil.
Or if you fear the outcome of matters, do not be afraid, for you have aimed for the goals of the fortunate.
Or if you have come to ask about a sick person, the Lord of Heaven has granted them a specific healing.
Or if you are in a legal dispute or traveling, O young man, you are victorious over your enemies.
Or if you are entering a partnership, or buying and selling, rise up, for your omen is one of great fortune.
Or if you sought the interpretation of a dream, it is good, guidance, and beautiful brilliance.
Or if you have come to ask about a righteous marriage, rejoice in the union with a beautiful and generous one.
The omen informs us with a true promise, in a text divided into poetic verses.
Alif <note>The first letter of the Arabic alphabet</note> is the letter that brings these glad tidings, so thank the God of the Throne, the Possessor of Blessings.

<column-break/>

Glad tidings! You have attained all your requests, your desires, and your pursuit of happiness.
The place of fortune has emerged, its signs have appeared, and justice and excellence have become clear through experience.
Hasten to the Chosen One <note>A reference to the Prophet Muhammad</note> regarding what you ask; what you seek is truth without falsehood.
The signs of glory and prosperity have appeared to you, so spring toward them, O you of pure lineage.
Sell, partner, litigate, and move, for you have attained what you hoped for without any weariness.
By God, do not hesitate in a legal case; do not fall short in resolve or in your goal.
The suns of the forenoon have appeared, rising with fortune, revolving as that which contains no ill.
Why the hesitation regarding a matter you are attempting? Rise to a rank that transcends all ranks.
The Generous Lord has cleared the way for you, so take an omen whose judgment is the most wondrous of wonders.
Through it, you shall gain acceptance and then honor from all the Turks, the Persians, and the Arabs.
With the letter Ba <note>The second letter of the alphabet</note>, the good news has arrived, and it deserves to be written on scrolls of pure gold.

---

# Discourse on the Letter Ta (T)
# Discourse on the Letter Tha (Th)

Your justice has appeared in all created things, while your envious enemy suffers in loss.
Goodness is abundant, and joy has arrived with fortune, striving from all directions.
Blessed be God the Almighty, who has given you beautiful attributes in this world.
Trade, marry, perform the pilgrimage, travel, grow, dwell, or move—do not fear any scattering of your affairs.
In this year, you shall visit the tomb of the Prophet Muhammad; welcome to the miracles!
You will find comfort in the morning light and in praise when you see your enemies and the envious in the throes of struggle.
You shall gain acceptance from all people and ascend to the highest of stations.
You shall be happy, honored, promoted, successful, and exalted; you shall be radiant and find yourself granted union with the "daughters" <note>Likely a metaphor for beautiful outcomes or literal marriage</note>.
You shall experience the attainment of desires and goals, as sweet as the dew on plants.
You shall cut through obstacles, reach your goals, command, find, judge, attain, be guided, be directed, and be exalted by receiving connections.
The letter Ta <note>The third letter of the alphabet</note> of the script has brought glad tidings, so thank Him who gives life to decayed bones.

<column-break/>

Trust in your affairs to God, the Inheritor; do not fear the plot of the treacherous envier.
You have tripled the light of the two luminaries <note>The sun and the moon</note> with a lunar appearance, so profit from it as a third.
Your eyes have been refreshed as they find comfort in your desires, and you are safe from the evil of the trifler.
Your roots are firm in happiness and high status; you have remained in glory, and what a fine dweller you are.
You have put on a new robe of happiness, so rise with the resolve of a hunting lion.
I have refined my script to stone the "Indians" <note>Likely a metaphor for enemies or obstacles</note> with a veil of justice, whether in new events or disasters.
Their heads have been brought low to you, as if they had sworn an oath and then committed perjury.
The swords of the lawmakers have been blunted, so do not fear, and place your certainty in God, the Inheritor.
The mothers of your enemies shall be bereaved; do not worry about anything, even if it seems to be growing.

You have humiliated your enemies and attained your desires, and you shall live your whole life in delight.

# Discourse on the Letter Za <note>The eleventh letter, equivalent to 'Z'.</note>

# Discourse on the Letter Sin <note>The twelfth letter, equivalent to 'S'.</note>

# Discourse on the Letter Ba <note>The second letter of the Arabic alphabet, used here as a key for bibliomancy or divination.</note>

May God and the Prophet accept you; the deputies of passing time shall accept you.
It is clear that this is a pleasant omen, bringing evidence of a prosperous life.
Your beloved shall reach out to you, so rise quickly to gather the Joseph-like beauty <note>A reference to the Prophet Joseph (Yusuf), who in Islamic tradition represents the pinnacle of human beauty.</note>.
Marriage suits you; propose and wed, so that the radiant face of the moon may be revealed.
O father of happiness, beauty strives to reach the Truth and the wealthy purse.
His praise wafts through all creation like the scent of musk and fragrant aloeswood.
God aids you with every goodness, with blessings, and with hidden grace.
The year shall be restored; you shall journey to the House <note>The Kaaba in Mecca</note> and visit the tomb of the Prophet.
He shall return to you the blessings of the Best of Creation, the Intercessor of Zamzam <note>Titles for the Prophet Muhammad; Zamzam refers to the holy well in Mecca.</note>.
May God lengthen your life in excellence and protect you from the evil of the wicked envious one.
The letter Ba gives tidings of luck, so rejoice; sustenance and a clever son have arrived.
Completed with the praise of God Almighty and His gracious success; praise be to God alone.

### Discourse on the Sign of Aries and Mars
The woman born under this ascendant <note>Arabic: *tali'*, the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> will have beautiful skin, face, and eyes. She will have children and marry two husbands, inheriting great wealth and blessings from the second. She is quick to anger but quick to forgive. Her best days are Sunday and Monday, and her most harmful is Friday. Most of her ailments will stem from "winds" <note>term: *arwah* (winds); in medieval medicine, this refers to gas, bloating, or wandering pains believed to be caused by vapors</note>, and her remedy is red sugar, jujube, and rosewater. She should be obedient to her husband. There is a fear for her life at age sixty-six, but her horoscope suggests she may live to eighty years. The one born under this sign should never cease the remembrance of God and should carry an amulet <note>term: *hirz*; a protective prayer or talisman</note> because she has many enemies and there is fear for her regarding the Evil Eye. God knows the unseen best and is most Wise.

### Discourse on the Sign of Taurus and Venus
The woman born under this sign will have a beautiful body and face. She loves conversing with people, has joined eyebrows, large eyes, and a fine stature. Female livestock are suitable for her. She will have one husband and many children. Most of her pains will be in the abdomen. She is sharp-tongued, quick to answer, and generally approachable. Her best day is Saturday, and her most harmful is Friday and the [first of the] months. It is best if her husband’s sign is Pisces or Cancer. Most of her ailments come from coldness, and her horoscope suggests she may pass away from an abdominal ailment. Her remedy is mastic, mastic, mastic <note>The word *mastaki* is repeated three times in the original text, likely for emphasis or as a scribal error</note>. If she suffers from a migraine, she should inhale the scent of Nile water and should not sleep until sunrise. She has a mole on her chest or back; if the mole is on her leg, she will be granted the pilgrimage to Mecca. There is fear for her at age seven and age twenty; if she survives these, she will live to seventy years. God knows the unseen best.

### Regarding the Judgment on the Sign of Gemini and Mercury
As for a woman born under this sign, she will be tall of stature with a beautiful face, though prone to vanity <note>original: *fajura*, implying boldness or transgressive behavior</note> and lacking patience during times of joy. She is quick-witted, sharp-tempered, and possesses good fortune. She will have a remedy for her husband's [troubles]. She has a hidden mole or mark and suffers from fear <unclear>at night</unclear> because she sees frightening dreams. She needs to have an amulet written for her containing the Names of God Almighty and a talisman against the ailments of <unclear>wind</unclear>. She may experience "winds" in her belly; she should use "cat-eye" suppositories <note>term: *ashyaf al-shananir*; likely a traditional medicinal preparation</note> and croton seeds <note>term: *habb al-muluq*; a potent laxative</note> if she wishes to <unclear>purge</unclear>. She should drink a decoction to induce menstruation if her flow is light. Her children will be male. She loves only through her own path and her own devotion, yet she has little luck with people. There is a fear of death for her at one year of age; if she survives, then at eleven years; if she survives that, she may live to seventy years, four months, and seven hours. God knows best.

### Discourse on the Sign of Cancer and the Moon
As for a woman born under this sign, she will have a healthy body, a beautiful form, and a complete intellect. She must marry a man through whom she will find great happiness, and she will be blessed with many children. When the new moon appears, she suffers from headaches; if it is summer, she should apply sandalwood to her head. In the world [of spirits] and the "heads of demons" <note>likely a reference to specific astrological or spiritual afflictions</note>, these will depart; garden cress and similar herbs will benefit her. She should take care of herself during pregnancy. Eating too much <unclear>food</unclear> or <unclear>sweets</unclear> does not suit her. She requires an amulet against the "falling sickness" <note>term: *al-qali'*; possibly referring to epilepsy or a specific childhood ailment</note> and rebellious demons, as there is fear for her regarding "transfers" <note>spiritual displacement</note> and common afflictions. She must have a talisman that she never removes unless she is in a state of ease. In her youth, she is at risk of falling from a high or difficult place. She has a mole or mark on her body. She has no luck from anyone and loves only for herself and her own regret. She has enemies. Her two sons will be of understanding, her commander of understanding, and after her hardship comes relief.

### Discourse on the Sign of Leo and the Sun
The sage Abu Ma'shar <note>Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi (787–886 AD) was a leading Persian astrologer in the Abbasid court, known in the West as Albumasar.</note> said: A woman born under this <term>ascendant</term> <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note> will have a beautiful face, a fair complexion, and sweet features. She has almond-shaped eyes, pleasant manners, a sweet way of speaking, a broad forehead, and a wide chest. She is broad-shouldered, strong-hearted, and possesses ample means of livelihood. She is married, loves jesting, and is free in her speech. Her <term>nature</term> <note>Referring to the four humors; Leo is a Fire sign.</note> is fiery and she is sharp-tempered; if she desires something, she cannot wait for it for even a single hour. She is fortunate, intelligent, and a mistress of cunning and stratagem. She is skilled in many arts and is modest. There will be a mole or a birthmark on her body. Her pain resides in her loins and limbs, and her remedy is the enema. She treats well those who treat her poorly. One should fear for her the <term>Evil Eye</term> <note>The belief that a malevolent glare can cause misfortune or injury.</note> and the envious glance. This written <term>amulet</term> <note>A protective prayer or charm.</note> should be hung upon her, which is the Opening of the Book <note>The Al-Fatiha, the first chapter of the Quran.</note> and the two "Refuge-taking" chapters <note>Surahs Al-Falaq and Al-Nas.</note>: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of sorcerers, madness, leprosy, the Evil Eye, and the glance of Jinn and men, and from the female spirits <note>Original: 'Al-Tawabi' and 'Umm al-Sibyan', spirits traditionally believed to afflict women and children.</note>, and from fevers, both new and old. God will suffice you against them, for He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." She is expected to live eighty-five years, and God knows best.

### Discourse on the Sign of Virgo and Mercury
The sage Abu Ma'shar said: A woman born under this ascendant will have a beautiful face, a good character, and a moderate stature. She is fair-skinned with a broad forehead, high-spirited, long-necked, and has a smiling set of teeth. She is very humorous, good in her deeds, meticulous, and prone to praising herself. She is sweet of speech, eloquent <note>Literally: 'moist of tongue'.</note>, and merciful of heart. <insert>Rejoice in tidings of good!</insert> Her life is pleasant; as her ascendant rises, her conditions improve. Her status will rise in the latter part of her life, and her wealth will increase. There will be a mark on her chest or her back. Her temperament is cold and dry <note>The qualities associated with the Earth element and the melancholic humor.</note>, and her remedy is everything warm and softening. She will have little luck with people, especially her husband; whenever she treats him well, he repays her with ugliness. In the middle of her life, she will attain prestige, wealth, and rank until people marvel at her good fortune. She is wise, possessing a keen intellect and understanding. She will have both enemies and friends, and men will love her more than women do. She will be prone to many illnesses and pains, so she should look after herself with a medicinal drink in every season. Fear for her from sorcery; this amulet should be hung upon her, which is the Chapter of the Opening, followed by: "I place the bearer of this writing of mine under the protection of God the Magnificent from the evil of every envious man and woman, and every plotter, male or female. And say: Truth has come and falsehood has vanished; surely falsehood is ever bound to vanish." She faces critical turning points <note>Original: 'Qutu' - astrological periods of danger to life.</note> in the fourth year of her life from a rising heat in her body, and in her fifteenth and fortieth years. If she survives these, she will live a long life, and God knows best.

### Discourse on the Sign of Libra and Venus
The sage Abu Ma'shar said: A woman born under this ascendant will have a beautiful face, a good character, and a moderate stature. She is wheat-colored <note>A light brown or tan complexion.</note>, slender-waisted, with a beautiful body and eyes. She is wise, intelligent, has a smiling set of teeth, is skilled in arts, and known for her generosity. She is beloved by those who see her; she is quick to anger but quick to be appeased.

### Discourse on the Sign of Scorpio and Mars

Abu Ma'shar <note>Albumasar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said: A woman born under this sign will have a beautiful face, a good character, a medium stature, black eyes, a wide forehead, and strong forearms. She is self-reliant, stout-hearted, but prone to boredom. She is soft-hearted, lacks patience, and does not remain in one state for long. She has a sharp temperament, is quick to answer, quick to anger, and quick to forgive. She loves herself and only loves those who provide for her; she takes from others but gives nothing of her own. As she grows older, her status increases. She has moles on her body and loves rest, leisure, play, and joking. Cold weather does not suit her; heat is better for her. Most of her pains come from her lower body, and vapors from her stomach rise to her head, causing heaviness. She should use remedies when she feels faint. I fear for her the "Evil Eye" and envious glances, as she has enemies and jealous people. The Chapter of the Opening <note>Al-Fatiha</note> should be written for her: "I seek refuge for the bearer of this writing of mine in God, besides whom there is no deity, Lord of the Great Throne. I seek refuge for her in the Lord of Gabriel and Israfel and the nearby angels of God, and by the right of these noble names: *Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh, Adonai, Tzabaot, El Shaddai*" <note>original: "باهيا اشراهيا ادوني اصباووت ايل شداي" - These are Hebrew names for God often used in Arabic magic and talismans</note>. I seek refuge for her from the evil of every possessor of evil, from the Eye, from the glance, and from the evil of calamities, defects, and trials, by the power of "There is no change or power except by God, the High, the Great." She faces a trial at four years of age; if she survives, then at fifteen; if she survives, then at forty; if she survives that, she will live to ninety-five years. God knows best.

### Discourse on the Sign of Sagittarius and Jupiter

The wise Abu Ma'shar said: A woman born under this sign will have a beautiful face, a good character, a tall stature, thick limbs, beautiful eyes and eyebrows, and pleasant speech. She is mature for her age, performs good deeds, is humble in her needs, has little greed, and possesses ample provisions. She keeps her clothes and body clean, is blessed with fortune, and is known for her goodness. She will receive compassion and love from a man of great status. The slightest thing breaks her heart, yet she continues to endure hardships. She has no luck from anyone else and remains modest and chaste, even regarding the shirt she wears. Whenever people envy her, God Almighty gives her more than them. In this month, she will have great joy and an increase in wealth.

## **Discourse on the Sign of Capricorn and Saturn**
The sage Abu Ma'shar <note>Ja'far ibn Muhammad Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi (787–886 AD), a famous Persian astrologer known in the West as Albumasar</note> said: A woman born under this ascendant <term>rising sign</term> will be brown-skinned, of clear complexion, with a fleshy face, a small nose and head. She is patient in the face of hardships, possesses much goodness, loves guests, and is pleasant in speech. She will have many children; from some of them, she will find great comfort, while others will cause her fatigue. They listen to her, yet they may face a trial regarding their livelihood. She will be a queen of her own destiny <note>literally "mistress of the unseen/future"</note>, and her wealth will not be under anyone else's hand. Everyone who sees her envies her for her rank and for her obedience in visiting the Sacred House of God <note>the Kaaba in Mecca</note> and visiting the grave of Muhammad, peace be upon him. As she grows older, her status and reputation will increase. She will have good fortune from her husband, though enemies may turn their faces from her. She should not be careless with her soul and should make something to ward off [evil] from her, for her nature is like the days—water flows beneath her while she remains fair. On her body, there is a mole or a birthmark. Whenever someone approaches her with kindness, God saves her through it, but whoever approaches her with force will not achieve their goal from her. She will suffer many illnesses; she should take a decoction of *jubbah* <note>possibly a botanical ingredient</note> and continue it on an empty stomach, following it with warm water, and she will be healed, God willing. She faces fear at night, so the Name of God should be hung upon her to protect against that. She faces a danger at twenty-five years and will live to be seventy years old. God knows best.

## **Discourse on the Sign of Aquarius and Saturn**
The sage Abu Ma'shar said: A woman born under this ascendant will have a fleshy face, thick eyebrows, a good character, long hair, light bones, and a round face. She loves to keep her secrets hidden always. She has little guile, speaks kindly to people, and has few children. Most of her pains come from backaches. Her temperament is hot and soft, and her remedy is everything soft and moderate. She will deal with inheritance among males and females. Back pain consumes them, so she should support her back. If she experiences a lack of affection, she should drink the "medicine of love." If she desires children, she should carry a wool [charm] and perfume herself. She should not sleep by her husband’s side on Sunday nights or Wednesday nights. She should say these three words during intimacy with the husband: "No patience for them, and he shall not tread upon another." It is: *Yaruh, Yaruh, Yaduh* <note>talismanic incantations</note>, put the love and affection of [Name] into the desire of [Name]. To protect against magic and the *Tabi'ah* <note>a female spirit or "follower" believed in folklore to cause miscarriages or illness</note>, she should hang [an amulet] upon herself.

**Discourse on the Sign of Pisces and Jupiter**

The sage Abu Ma'shar <note>Albumasar (787–886 AD), a famous Persian astrologer whose works were influential in both the Islamic world and Europe</note> said: The woman born under this ascendant will be beautiful of face, good-natured, and fond of amusement, play, and laughter. She has a broad forehead, a long neck, a round face, and beautiful eyes. By temperament, she loves joy and happiness; she is fair-skinned, has thin hair, and is intelligent and discerning. She may complain of pain but will rejoice after <unclear>overcoming</unclear> her illness. She will be granted a high rank among the elite and will have <unclear>in</unclear> and a white mark upon her belly. She will be of moderate standing among <unclear>people</unclear>, and those who know her will find her one who fulfills the needs of others. She finds goodness in the needs of her soul, and <unclear>emerges</unclear> from it. It is fitting that she wears an iron ring on her hand. Regarding the <unclear>evil</unclear> of enemies who enter her life, she should act to turn their faces away from her. Her lot of fortune comes at twenty years and thirty years; if she passes these, she shall live a long life. God knows best the unseen and the appointed term.

Whoever seeks the sea of love in their horoscope <note>The original is in Ottoman Turkish: "Her kiminki tale'i bahr-i 'ashka talib ise"</note>

The command: subtract the total from itself and look at the remainder. <note>This refers to a mathematical operation used in divination to find a remainder (modulus).</note>
By this calculation, it will be known which zodiac sign a person's horoscope falls under.
</insert>

Abu Ubayd Allah al-Mahalli said: *Abujad, Hawwaz, Hutti, Kalamani, Sa'fas,* and *Qarasht* <note>These are the mnemonic names for the Abjad sequence of the alphabet.</note> were the kings of Midian. Their supreme king during the time of the Prophet Shu'ayb <note>The biblical Jethro</note>—specifically during the "Day of the Shadow" <note>A Quranic event where a cloud brought fire or heat as punishment.</note>—was *Kalamun*. When he perished, his daughter wept for him, saying:

"Kalamun has demolished my pillar;
The master of the people perished in the heart of the camp.
Death came to him, calling beneath his canopy.
Fire was set upon them, leaving their home like a fading mist;
So they became, in their dwellings, prostrate."
— *The Landmarks of Revelation* <note>original: "Ma'alim al-Tanzil," a famous Quranic commentary by al-Baghawi.</note>

<summary>This page presents a table for the "Small Abjad" numerological system and recounts a legendary history of the Arabic alphabet's mnemonic names as ancient kings of Midian. It includes marginal notes in Ottoman Turkish regarding astrological calculations and the "sea of love."</summary>
<keywords>Abjad, numerology, Midian, Kalamun, Shu'ayb, astrology, horoscopes, Ma'alim al-Tanzil, Arabic alphabet origins</keywords>
